title: The three days
summary: Each gospel sets the crucifixion on the day of Preparation and has the women find the tomb empty early on the first day of the week, a Sunday. How that makes 'the third day', and 'three days and three nights' (Matt 12:40), depends on the weekday of the crucifixion, which is read three ways; the chart draws whichever is chosen in the Days tab. The readings draw on two ways of counting. A Jewish day ran from sunset to sunset, so the Sabbath began on Friday evening (Luke 23:54). And the Talmud counts part of a day as a whole day (Pesachim 4a); Esther's fast of 'three days, night or day' ends 'on the third day' (Esth 4:16–5:1), and in Matthew the chief priests say both 'after three days' and 'until the third day' (27:63–64).
clock: Clock times are ≈. In Jerusalem near the spring equinox, when Passover falls, sunrise and sunset are close to 6 a.m. and 6 p.m., and the gospels count the hours of the day from sunrise, so 'the third hour' is about 9 a.m. and 'the ninth hour' about 3 p.m. These are derived figures: an hour was a twelfth of the daylight, near the equinox about a clock hour.

died.basis: Jesus cries out 'at the ninth hour' and then breathes his last (Mark 15:34–37); the ninth hour is ≈3 p.m.

buried.basis: Buried when 'it was already evening' on the day before the Sabbath (Mark 15:42–46), as 'the Sabbath was beginning' (Luke 23:54): before sunset, ≈6 p.m.

readings.label: Friday

rose.basis: The text never says when he rose. The tomb was already empty when Mary Magdalene came 'while it was still dark' (John 20:1), and 'the third day' begins at sunset on Saturday, so the chart shades that night.

readings.basis: Mark calls the day of the crucifixion 'Preparation Day (that is, the day before the Sabbath)' (15:42), and Luke has the women rest on the Sabbath and come to the tomb on the first day of the week with no day between (23:54–24:1). John's 'High Sabbath' (19:31) is then the weekly Sabbath falling in the Passover week.
readings.thirdDay: Friday is the first day, the Sabbath the second, Sunday the third: counted inclusively, as Esther's 'three days' end 'on the third day' (Esth 4:16–5:1).
readings.nights: Only two nights, Friday's and Saturday's. The reading takes 'three days and three nights' as an idiom for the same inclusive span, a part of a day counting as a whole day and night; Matthew himself sets 'after three days' beside 'until the third day' (27:63–64).
traditions: The church's observance of Good Friday and Easter since the early centuries

readings.label: Thursday

rose.basis: As in the Friday reading: after sunset on Saturday, and before Mary Magdalene came 'while it was still dark' (John 20:1).

readings.basis: John's 'High Sabbath' (19:31) is taken as the first day of Unleavened Bread, a day of rest whatever its weekday (Lev 23:6–7), falling on Friday, with the weekly Sabbath after it. Two Sabbaths in a row leave Thursday for the crucifixion.
readings.thirdDay: Counted inclusively from Thursday, Sunday is the fourth day. The reading has to count 'the third day' from the day after the crucifixion: Friday, Saturday, Sunday.
readings.nights: Thursday, Friday and Saturday nights: three nights, and three daylights (Thursday's last hours, Friday, Saturday), before a rising on Sunday before dawn.

sources.note: the first day of Unleavened Bread a day of rest

sources.author: Harold W. Hoehner

readings.label: Wednesday

rose.basis: The reading has him rise just before sunset on Saturday, 72 hours after a burial just before sunset on Wednesday; the tomb was already empty when the women came on Sunday.

readings.basis: John's 'High Sabbath' (19:31) is the first day of Unleavened Bread (Lev 23:6–7), on Thursday, and the weekly Sabbath follows on Saturday with Friday between. The reading finds that working day in Mark and Luke: the women buy spices 'when the Sabbath was over' (Mark 16:1), prepare them, and then rest 'on the Sabbath, according to the commandment' (Luke 23:56).
readings.thirdDay: Counted inclusively from Wednesday, Sunday is the fifth day. The reading counts 'the third day since these things took place' (Luke 24:21) from something later, such as the guard set at the tomb the next day (Matt 27:62–66).
readings.nights: Wednesday, Thursday and Friday nights, and Thursday, Friday and Saturday daylight: three days and three nights taken literally, 72 hours.

Mark.16.1.basis: After the High Sabbath ended at sunset on Thursday; the reading has them buy spices then or on Friday.

Luke.23.56.basis: The spices prepared on Friday, the working day between the two Sabbaths, and the rest kept on Saturday.
